thread:
Alice Nguyen: heads up — deploy to prod started ~1749991200, canary 1/3 is showing traffic but the canary metrics dashboard is empty for request_latency.svc_redwood — just zeros. not seeing error spikes in logs though.
Bob Singh: seeing the same from my side. noisy alerts kicked in for 5xx rate but dashboard panels are empty? that smells like a tag/name mismatch or metrics pipeline filter.
Carol Tanaka: rolling out a small FF: feature_flag=fast_path_v3. I didn't change metrics names. I pushed the flag at 1749991100.
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2025-331. PagerDuty notified to alice.nguyen and bob.singh.
Sean Miller: customers on the beta org reported slow responses ~1749991300. any direct errors in gateway?
Alice Nguyen: gateway logs show 200s but tail latency shifted for a small shard. attaching short snippet: ```
[1749991298] svc_redwood request_id=abc123 latency_ms=420
[1749991299] svc_redwood request_id=abc124 latency_ms=480
```
Bob Singh: I think the alerts were based on metric tag service:svc=redwood, but the canary instances are shipping service:app=redwood (tag rename). the metrics pipeline used a strict filter so panels look empty but alert rules still evaluated on the raw metric stream, hence noisy pagers.
Carol Tanaka: oh wow — I changed the exporter config in the build to standardize tags. that was in the canary image. i can revert the tag change in the exporter and roll the canary back if needed.
Alice Nguyen: impact sketch: SLO tokenized latency for alpha customers spiked to P95 ~420ms for ~8m. some retries visible in product logs. not seeing 5xx surge.
Bob Singh: mitigation options: 1) quick rollback of canary to previous exporter (fast) 2) rollback the FF 3) patch alert rules to include the new tag mapping (takes longer) 4) temporary silence of noisy alerts.
Carol Tanaka: i recommend kill the FF first — least invasive. issuing kill now. `/ff kill fast_path_v3 --env=prod --reason="canary tag mismatch, noisy alerts and metric gaps"`
Alice Nguyen: confirm when FF kill completed.
Incident Bot: Feature flag kill executed by Carol Tanaka at 1749991390.
PagerDuty: Pager sent to on-call for 2nd tier. Escalation policy started.
Bob Singh: FF kill acknowledged. I still want the canary auto-rollout stopped — carol can you pause the deploy pipeline?
Carol Tanaka: paused canary pipeline at 1749991410. rolling back the image to previous SHA now.
Sean Miller: customer support says one paying customer reported increased latency for ~10 minutes — flagged for outreach if rollback doesn't improve in next 5.
Alice Nguyen: I'm going to mute the noisy alert group (alert:svc_redwood_5xx_rate) for 10m while we validate. temp silence applied 1749991420.
Bob Singh: while alerts are muted, i'm streaming metrics from the exporter directly: i can see request_latency.svc_redwood with tags app=redwood (new) and svc=redwood (old) both exist during transition window. dashboard panels needed a query tweak — they were pinned to svc only.
Carol Tanaka: rollback completed at 1749991503. canary instances now back on previous exporter config.
Alice Nguyen: dashboards repopulating — panels showing P50/P95 now. latency trending back to baseline.
Bob Singh: unwinding: unmute alerts in 5m if metrics stable. Also we need a postmortem action: don't change metric tag schema in canary without staging metric pipeline validation.
Sean Miller: customer outreach queued to support, we'll offer a short incident note. only one org impacted, no data loss.
Incident Bot: Incident INC-2025-331 status changed to "mitigated" at 1749991600.
Carol Tanaka: quick follow-up: the tag rename was intended to standardize across services. i'll open a PR to make the metric exporter compatible with both tag keys and add a gating test to rollout checklist.
Bob Singh: action items: (1) add metric tag compatibility test to CI (owner: Bob) (2) add canary observability checklist requiring metrics validation (owner: Carol) (3) update alert rules to be resilient to tag renames or use service_id (owner: Alice).
Alice Nguyen: assigning and putting short timelines in the incident doc. also recommend a short blameless postmortem tomorrow with timeline and customer impact.
Sean Miller: sounds good. closing loop with support and scheduled follow-up at 1749991800 for final verification.
Alice Nguyen: final note — thanks everyone for quick triage. main root cause: tag rename in canary exporter + strict dashboard/alert filters => metrics appeared missing while alerts still fired. learned: metric schema changes must be opt-in behind feature gates and validated by canary observability smoke tests. :white_check_mark:
